newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Slain Zaire general was to meet Kabila, diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Slain Zaire general was to meet Kabila, diplomat.

text.p: Zaire's army chief, killed by presidential guards in Kinshasa on Friday night, was supposed to meet rebel leader Laurent Kabila in the Zambian capital on Saturday to discuss a transition of power, a diplomat said.

"General Mahele was to meet Kabila this morning in Lusaka to discuss a handover of power. It was a deal brokered by the United States," said the clearly disappointed diplomat, who declined to be identified.

General Mahele Lieko Bokungu, defence minister and chief of army staff, was killed late on Friday by presidential guards at Camp Tshatshi, the Kinshasa army barracks residence of Mobutu who flew to his northern palace at Gbadolite earlier on Friday.

A senior western diplomat in Kinshasa told Reuters the general was killed by the Special Presidential Division (DSP). Some sources said he went to the camp with regular army units to bring DSP members under control.

The United States with South Africa were at the forefront of diplomatic efforts to avoid a bloody showdown in Kinshasa. U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday urged the world to support South African President Nelson Mandela's efforts for peace.
